newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO SLASH BULGING TRADE GAP IN 1997-PM.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO SLASH BULGING TRADE GAP IN 1997-PM.

text.p: Romania's Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Friday that his centrist coalition government would slash the ex-communist country's bulging trade gap in 1997, seeking renewed funds from international lenders.
"The foreign trade balance deficit will be cut to $1.4 billion in 1997, from $2.5 billion in 1996," Ciorbea told a meeting with leaders of his National Peasant Party.
He did not say if the trade gap figures were in FOB of CIF prices. Latest trade data, in FOB prices, put Romania's 1996 trade deficit at $1.54 billion, against 1995's $1.57 billion.
Ciorbea said that his government was on the point of completing loan talks with the International Monetary Fund and had ended parallel negotiations with the World Bank.
He did not give further details on the loan package.

The new centrist coalition, which ousted ex-communists in elections last November has vowed to speed up reforms in order to renew credits from both lenders who had suspended funds for Romania last year.
Over the past two years Romania has been saddled with big trade deficits, and experienced pains in finding sources to finance those gaps.
Attempts by the former leftist government to keep the leu aritficially high in an election year last year led to a decline in exports, which fell by 3.2 percent from 1995.
Ciorbea said he would detail a set of sweeping economic reforms, coupled with social protection steps, during a news conference next Monday.
